comment: The vectors pinning Prima.WorkerAPI as it crosses HTTP (Prima.WorkerWire): every request CYFR makes of a worker service, signed with the dispatch key of tests/fixtures/worker_auth.json under its fields (Prima.WorkerAuth.request_header/3) and posted plain, and its plain answer. Every body and answer carries v, the wire version, as its first member; a body whose v is absent or not version is unknown_version before its op is read, and an answer without it, or at another, is a lost answer. refusals are the answers each request may be given instead, at their HTTP status, with why: a 503 is a refusal of a start only when it names a sentence, or for room when it carries what holds the memory (held, Prima.LocusPool's one form), and is otherwise a lost answer. status holds the vectors of a status answer's value. max_body_bytes is the most a request body spans and window_ms how far a header's ts may be from the listener's clock. request_bodies are bodies each read as a WorkerAPI callback (Prima.WorkerWire.read_request_body/2): its callback and args, or its error, the version read before anything else; one marked go is the two ends' stated difference, a body Prima reads at any depth that a Go reader refuses nested past 4,096 (go's error), each side's test asserting its own answer. answers are answers each read as Prima.WorkerWire.read_answer/1 reads them: ok and its value, error with its name and every other member kept as its fields, or lost. answer_writes are the bytes Prima.WorkerWire.ok/1, error/2 and request_body/2 write: v first, a refusal's fields by name with any named v or error dropped, a plain map's members by name. base_urls are texts read as Prima.WorkerWire.base_url/1 reads them, to their base or null, their parts as URI.parse/1 reads them. max_report_attempts is Prima.WorkerWire.max_report_attempts/0. keeper_refusals are what a worker service holds for the keeper's refusal of a runner's spawn, by the code the keeper sent (Prima.WorkerAPI.keeper_refusal/1, which the Elixir service gives memory_unavailable as the atom Locus.Keeper reads it to and no_memory with the keeper's held), the keeper's held carried beside a no_memory, which a start refused for room answers: the reason and the sentence a start refused for it and a status carry; the case of no code is the Elixir service's alone (elixir_only), since every code the keeper sends is text. report_refusals are the codes a report's refusal may carry (Prima.WorkerAPI.runner_refusal/1 names a sentence for each carried one) and some it may not. nonces are presentations to one listener's nonce table in order (Locus.Listener.fresh/4, window_ms 30,000): a nonce is fresh at its first presentation and refused for two windows from it, until 60,000 ms past it, and fresh again after. listener are requests each made of the runtime's worker listener over HTTP (http: run against the listener itself), in the order its refusals are decided: method and path, the path matched as the request spells it, its query apart, the header (none, twice, at another version, not parsing, out of the window, under another key, another service, a nonce seen before), the body bounded to max_body_bytes and checked against its header, then its JSON, version and callback, and each callback's args; header is how the request is signed: signed, by this service's dispatch key at the listener's clock (ts_offset_ms from it, service in place of its own), none, twice, v2 (its version token replaced), text (header_text), other_key, other_body (naming another body), replay (the same header sent first on the connection with another body, which the listener refuses bad_mac and keeps the connection) or replay_answered (its nonce presented first by a request it answered); credentials false makes the request of a service holding none; body is its json, its text or a size of bytes; before_body is answered before a byte of the body is sent; requests are several made one after another on one connection, each answered as it says; status and answer are the answer's, byte for byte (or reading ok for a status), and closes whether the connection is closed after it, a connection kept answering a status next. starts are starts each made with the args CYFR would send for this service and boot (assignment, input, sealed_keys) and start's change: a member dropped, an input that is no text, an assignment for another boot or service or that does not read, an input other than the one its digest names or no JSON object, keys that open as another attempt or not at all, or a member more; each is answered 200 with answer, and only the last runs. An exit of the call into the service is answered 503 unavailable without a sentence, and is not here: no request makes one.

status.comment: The answer of Prima.WorkerAPI's status as its listener writes it: the contracts suite reads every valid wire to its status and writes that status back to exactly the same wire, and refuses every invalid one; the worker image tests' control plane (tests/locus-runtime-image/worker_auth.py) reads the same. memory_bytes is the bound every runner runs under, null where the keeper applies none; refusal is why the keeper refuses runners, null while it starts them.
